subject: Biology
description: Trachea, bronchi, alveoli, gas exchange, lung volumes, common diseases

questions.stem: Gas exchange in human lungs occurs at the:

options.option_text: Alveoli (tiny air sacs surrounded by capillaries)

questions.explanation: Alveoli — ~300-500 million per pair of lungs, providing surface area ~70-100 m² (about half a tennis court). Single-cell-thick wall (Type I pneumocytes) in close contact with capillaries → fast O₂/CO₂ diffusion. Type II pneumocytes secrete surfactant — reduces surface tension, prevents alveolar collapse (premature babies often deficient → respiratory distress syndrome, treated with exogenous surfactant). Trachea, bronchi, bronchioles — only conducting (no gas exchange).
questions.diagram_hint: Cross-section of human lungs showing trachea → primary bronchi → secondary → tertiary → bronchioles → alveolar sacs with capillary network. Inset: single alveolus with O₂/CO₂ exchange arrows.

questions.stem: The diaphragm — main muscle of breathing — is which type of muscle?

options.option_text: Skeletal (under both involuntary and voluntary control)

questions.explanation: Diaphragm — dome-shaped skeletal muscle separating thoracic and abdominal cavities. Innervated by phrenic nerve (cervical roots C3-C5 — 'C3, 4, 5 keep the diaphragm alive'). Contraction → flattens → expands chest cavity → creates negative pressure → air drawn in (INSPIRATION). Relaxation → recoils → expiration. External intercostals also contract during inspiration. Although skeletal, breathing rhythm is automatic (medulla's respiratory centre) — but voluntary control is possible (holding breath, hyperventilating). Hiccups = involuntary diaphragm spasms.

questions.stem: Average resting respiratory rate (breaths per minute) of an adult human is:
questions.explanation: Adult resting: 12-20 breaths/min (typical 16). Newborn: 30-60. Children: 18-30. Athletic adults at rest: as low as 8. During exercise: 30-50. Tachypnea (>20) — fever, anxiety, asthma, pneumonia. Bradypnea (<12) — sedation, opioid overdose. Tidal Volume ~500 mL per breath at rest; ~3-6 L during exercise. Total ventilation = TV × RR = 500 × 16 ≈ 8 L/min at rest. Normal SpO₂ (oxygen saturation) ≥ 95%.

questions.stem: Oxygen is transported in blood mainly by:

options.option_text: Haemoglobin (in red blood cells) — ~98.5% of total O₂ transport

questions.explanation: Each Hb molecule carries 4 O₂ (binding to iron in heme). 1 g of Hb binds ~1.34 mL O₂. Normal Hb concentration: 12-16 g/dL → arterial blood ~20 mL O₂/100 mL. Only ~1.5% of O₂ is dissolved in plasma (gives PaO₂ measurement). Cooperative binding (S-shaped Hb-O₂ dissociation curve) means Hb readily picks up O₂ in lungs (high pO₂) and unloads in tissues (low pO₂). CO₂ transport — different: ~70% as bicarbonate (in plasma + RBC), ~23% bound to Hb (as carbamino-Hb), ~7% dissolved.

questions.stem: Total Lung Capacity (TLC) of a healthy adult man is approximately:
questions.explanation: TLC = ~5-6 L in adult male, ~4-5 L in female. Components — Vital Capacity (VC, max breath cycle ~4.5 L) + Residual Volume (RV, ~1.2 L, can't be exhaled). VC = Tidal Volume (TV ~500 mL) + Inspiratory Reserve (IRV ~3 L) + Expiratory Reserve (ERV ~1.1 L). FEV1 — forced expiratory volume in 1 sec; FEV1/FVC ratio normally >0.7. <0.7 → obstructive (asthma, COPD); both reduced → restrictive (fibrosis). Spirometry tests these.

questions.stem: Asthma is best classified as a/an:

options.option_text: Obstructive lung disease — reversible airway narrowing due to inflammation + bronchoconstriction

questions.explanation: Asthma — chronic inflammatory disorder; airway hyper-responsiveness; reversible obstruction. Symptoms: wheeze, dyspnea, cough, chest tightness — episodic; triggered by allergens, exercise, cold air, infection, stress. Bronchoconstriction + mucus plugging + inflammation. Treatment: SABA (salbutamol) for relief; ICS (inhaled corticosteroids — budesonide, fluticasone) + LABA (formoterol, salmeterol) for prevention. WHO estimates ~262 million asthmatics globally; India ~3-4 crore. World Asthma Day — first Tuesday of May. Other obstructive: COPD (chronic, irreversible — 90% smoking related). Restrictive — fibrosis, sarcoidosis (lung volume reduced).

questions.stem: Cellular respiration (glucose + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O + ATP) NET produces approximately how many ATP per glucose?
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration of one glucose: Glycolysis (cytoplasm) — 2 ATP net + 2 NADH. Pyruvate oxidation — 2 NADH. Krebs cycle (mitochondrial matrix) — 2 ATP + 6 NADH + 2 FADH₂. Oxidative phosphorylation (inner mitochondrial membrane, ETC + chemiosmosis) — each NADH → ~2.5 ATP, each FADH₂ → ~1.5 ATP. Total ≈ 30-32 ATP. Older textbook value 38 used 3 ATP/NADH + 2 ATP/FADH₂; modern P/O ratios revised lower. Anaerobic glycolysis (no O₂) — only 2 ATP per glucose (much less efficient) → why we tire from sprinting.
